map.基于 Cotswold 修订的 Ann Arbor 分期系统，适用于霍奇金和非霍: Based on the Cotswold-revised Ann Arbor staging system, for Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma
map.按受累淋巴结区与横膈关系定 Ann Arbor 分期（I–IV）: Set the Ann Arbor stage (I–IV) by the involved lymph node regions and their relation to the diaphragm
map.加注 A/B 症状、结外(E)、脾(S)、巨块(X) 修饰: Add the A/B symptom, extranodal (E), splenic (S) and bulky (X) modifiers
map.区分霍奇金与 NHL 的治疗策略差异: Distinguish treatment strategy differences between Hodgkin and NHL
map.：Ann Arbor（Cotswold 修订）：I 单个淋巴结区；II 横膈同侧: : Ann Arbor (Cotswold revision): I a single lymph node region; II at least 2 regions on the same side of the diaphragm; III both sides of the diaphragm; IV diffuse extranodal involvement. Modifiers: A absent / B present systemic symptoms (fever above 38 °C, night sweats, weight loss above 10% within 6 months), E localized extranodal, S splenic involvement, X bulky (mediastinal ratio at least 1/3 or mass at least 10 cm).
map.：例1（横膈上 2 个淋巴结区、无 B 症状）：IIA 期（局限进展期）。例2（: : example 1 (2 lymph node regions above the diaphragm, no B symptoms): stage IIA (limited progression). Example 2 (1 region above plus 1 below the diaphragm): stage III (both sides of the diaphragm). Example 3 (multiple extranodal organs plus bulky disease): stage IV (advanced). Treatment escalates from radiotherapy/chemotherapy to autologous transplant across stages.
map.巨块型 X 为什么单独标？: Why is bulky disease X marked separately?
map.巨块（纵隔比≥1/3 或最大径≥10 cm）预后较差、局部复发风险高，常需巩固放: Bulky disease (mediastinal ratio at least 1/3 or maximum diameter at least 10 cm) has poorer prognosis and higher local recurrence risk, often needing consolidation radiotherapy or intensive chemotherapy, so X is appended after the stage to guide radiotherapy decisions.
map.B 症状一定代表晚期吗？: Do B symptoms necessarily mean advanced stage?
map.不一定。B 症状是预后不良因素但与分期独立；早期（I/II）伴 B 症状仍归相应: Not necessarily. B symptoms are an adverse prognostic factor but independent of stage; early stage (I/II) with B symptoms is still staged as early, only treated more aggressively (often handled as 'unfavorable early stage').
